modules.title: 15 components, two doors, one platform
modules.lede: Read it as two lanes: what the police do with a record, and what an employer gets when they ask. Door B has no path to the registry, the map or the case record.

items.name: Police & women safety teams
items.summary: Officers who register cases, review records, receive alerts and verify addresses in the field, within their own rank and jurisdiction.

details.label: Takes in

details.label: Produces
details.text: Case entries, field outcomes, review decisions

details.label: If it fails

items.name: Officer app
items.summary: The officer-facing application: registry, case records, alerts, assignments and field capture, on desktop and on a phone.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Officer session; assigned work

details.label: Produces
details.text: Record views, field reports, status updates

details.label: If it fails
details.text: Field capture queues on the device when offline and syncs when the signal returns.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: The systems that own the facts: police records, the prison service and the courts, all reached through one managed gateway so authentication and retries are solved once.

details.label: Produces
details.text: Authorised queries and events

details.label: If it fails
details.text: Cases, custody events, court orders and status changes

items.name: Case record
items.summary: Each case against the profile: station, dates, the exact sections it was registered under, and whether it belongs in the registry at all.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Case data from the justice systems; officer updates

details.label: Produces
details.text: Case records with their exact legal provisions

details.label: If it fails
details.text: An unrecognised provision is flagged for configuration, not quietly included or dropped.

items.name: Legal status
items.summary: One current status per case — accused, under trial, convicted, released, acquitted — each with where it came from and when.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Court and prison events; officer updates

details.label: Produces
details.text: A status per case, with its source

details.label: If it fails
details.text: Conflicting events are held for review. The platform never decides a status on its own.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Follows admission, sentence, transfer, release, bail and parole, so the day someone is released is known before it happens, not after.

details.label: Produces
details.text: Prisoner lifecycle events

details.label: If it fails
details.text: A custody timeline; release and interim-release events

items.name: Alerts & field work
items.summary: Works out which station covers the verified address, sends the alert to that women safety team with a due date, and records what the officer found on the visit.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Status and release events; addresses; station boundaries

details.label: Produces
details.text: Routed alerts, assignments and visit outcomes

details.label: If it fails
details.text: If no station can be resolved the alert escalates to district supervision rather than being dropped.

items.name: Schools & employers
items.summary: Schools, universities, childcare bodies, hospitals and corporations. All registered, all authenticated, all held to one identical limit.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: A verification request, with consent

details.label: Produces
details.text: One permitted outcome, with a reference number

details.label: If it fails
details.text: An unregistered or lapsed requester is refused before a request is even created.

items.name: Request portal
items.summary: The separate requester-facing application. It can submit a request and track it. It cannot search, browse or view a record.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Requester session; request form and consent document

details.label: Produces
details.text: Request status; the issued response

details.label: If it fails
details.text: An incomplete request is rejected at submission with a reason, before it is routed anywhere.

items.name: Disclosure gate
items.summary: The decision that stands between a request and any answer. Identical for a village school and a national corporation.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: The request, consent, role, officer review, record status

details.label: Produces
details.text: One permitted outcome, or a refusal with a reason

details.label: If it fails
details.text: Any condition unresolved means no disclosure — and the attempt is still logged in full.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Produces the referenced response the requester receives. It carries an outcome and a reference number — never an extract of the record.

details.label: Produces
details.text: The gate decision; the request reference

details.label: If it fails
details.text: A signed response with a reference number

items.name: Sign-in & permissions
items.summary: Decides which door a person enters and what is reachable once inside. This is where the two sides are kept apart.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Credentials, role, rank, unit, jurisdiction, organisation

details.label: Produces
details.text: A scoped session; a permission decision on every action

details.label: If it fails
details.text: A failed or unclear authorisation denies by default, and the attempt is logged.

items.name: Records & audit
items.summary: One store for profiles, cases, events and requests — and an immutable record of every view, search, decision and disclosure.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Writes and access events from everything above

details.label: Produces
details.text: Records with provenance; an exportable audit trail

details.label: If it fails
details.text: If the audit path is down the action is refused. Nothing happens unrecorded.

items.name: Seven reports
items.tag: What it all adds up to
items.summary: Turns registry, custody, field and verification activity into the seven operational reports.

details.label: Takes in
details.text: Records and events from the store

details.label: Produces

details.label: If it fails

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
The record already exists. It is never in one place at the right time. The report sits in crime records, the trial in the court system, the sentence in prison records — so one individual across three cases becomes three unconnected records, and the pattern never surfaces.

Why it exists

The person is scattered

One individual across three systems becomes three unconnected records.

Now · one master profile, many linked cases

Release passes unnoticed

An offender completes a sentence and returns to a jurisdiction where no officer was told. The information existed — it never reached the station that needed it.

Now · release events raise a routed alert

Employers have no lawful route

A school hiring a bus driver has documents and references and no proper way to ask the police anything — so either nothing is checked, or records move through channels that should not exist.

Now · one consented, audited, gated channel

Two operational ecosystems · same platform, separate access, identical limit

Door A · lawful authority

Police & field team operations

The operational registry: identify, register and track individuals connected to sexual-offence cases, with legal status maintained accurately at every stage.

  • Consolidated registry of case-linked individuals
  • Accused, under-trial and convicted kept as distinct categories
  • Release, bail and legal-status change alerts
  • Verified addresses, geotagged and jurisdiction-resolved
  • Repeat-offender and multi-case identification
  • Field assignments and follow-up history
Women safety teamsPolice stations Investigating officersDistrict supervision
Door B · controlled disclosure

Institutional & employer verification

A segregated portal where registered requesters submit consented background-verification requests for people in roles with access to women and children — and receive an outcome against a defined scope.

  • Requester registration and authentication
  • Consent and authorisation captured with every request
  • Requests routed to the correct police jurisdiction
  • An authorised officer reviews before any response is issued
  • Outcome returned as a referenced verification certificate
  • Full request and access history retained for audit
SchoolsUniversitiesChildcare HospitalsCorporationsTransport staffing
No requester goes beyond the limit — corporations included

There is no enhanced tier. A corporation is held to exactly the same gate, the same scope and the same outcome set as a primary school, whatever its size, sector, contract value or stated reason. Size does not buy access, and neither does a commercial relationship with the department.

No search or browseNo case file No accused recordNo victim information No map or monitoring viewNo bulk or standing access

The disclosure gate · five conditions, all true or no disclosure

A verification response leaves the platform only when every one of five conditions is true. They are evaluated with AND — one false is enough to stop a response. The gate is identical for every requester: the conditions evaluated, the scope of the check and the outcome text are byte-identical between a school and a corporate requester. The only thing that differs in the record is which registered requester asked, and that is kept for audit, not used to widen what is returned.

Nineteen stages take one individual end to end — a case registered, a profile matched, a conviction and sentence, a release that raises an alert, a field verification, and finally an employer's question answered at the gate. Seventeen scenarios cover identity matching, split legal statuses, acquittals, bail and parole, address changes, failed field visits, refused disclosures and victim-protected cases.

Safeguards · useful to the officer, fair to the individual

  • Victim identity protected — victim information is restricted throughout and never leaves through Door B.
  • Due process preserved — accused, under-trial and convicted stay separate in the data model, the workflows and every disclosure. A pending report is never returned as a finding.
  • Access is narrow and logged — role-based by rank, unit and jurisdiction, with an immutable record of every view, search, download and disclosure.
  • Consent and a human reviewer — no verification runs without recorded consent, and no response is issued without an authorised officer deciding what is disclosable.
  • Provenance on every field — each record carries its source system, verification status and last-updated time.
  • Monitoring within authority — geotagging an address is not live tracking, and release is not surveillance. Each assignment records the order it acts on.
  • Structural separation — Door B has no path to the registry, the map or the case record. The boundary is in the architecture, not in a permission setting someone can widen.
